title: Constant-time padding validation in a CBC unpad kernel
objective: Rewrite the pad_check kernel in inputs/cbc_unpad.cpp so that it inspects the final decrypted block and returns both a validity flag and the unpadded plaintext length, while performing a full, uniform scan of the block on every call regardless of the padding contents. The revised kernel must be a drop-in replacement that keeps the exact function signature and file location, is synthesizable-style C++ (no dynamic allocation, no STL containers, no exceptions), and must compile standalone with g++ against a test harness that calls it directly.
interface: File: inputs/cbc_unpad.cpp. Entry point (must match exactly, no overloads, no namespaces): void pad_check(const unsigned char block[16], int *valid, int *unpadded_len); block is a 16-byte array representing the final decrypted CBC block. valid is an output pointer that must be set to 1 if the padding is well-formed PKCS#7 padding (last byte N in range 1..16 and the last N bytes of block all equal N), or 0 otherwise. unpadded_len is an output pointer that must be set to 16 - N when *valid == 1, and to 16 when *valid == 0. The function must not read or write memory outside block[0..15] and the two output pointers, must not call malloc/new, must not throw, and must return normally (void) in all cases.
constraints: Do not change the function name, signature, parameter order, or the file path inputs/cbc_unpad.cpp.
Do not use dynamic memory allocation, STL containers, or C++ exceptions.
The implementation must be pure C/C++ compilable with g++ without additional libraries.
Do not add any additional side-effecting output parameters or global state.
expected_outputs: A revised inputs/cbc_unpad.cpp implementing the pad_check kernel with the pinned signature, returning correct validity and unpadded length for all block contents, compiling cleanly with g++, and scanning the full 16-byte block in a uniform, content-independent manner on every invocation.
submission_contract: Participants submit a hardened, secure version of inputs/cbc_unpad.cpp. The evaluator grades that file in place: a correctly hardened implementation passes, while the originally shipped baseline implementation fails.

metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of targeted weakness classes for which the submitted kernel exhibits detectable data-dependent iteration/comparison-count variation across adversarial mismatch-position test vectors.

metrics.name: information_flow_correctness
metrics.description: Whether the observable behavioral signal (instrumented loop/comparison count) is provably invariant across all tested padding/mismatch configurations while validity and length outputs remain correct.

metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of functional and behavioral test cases for which the compiled binary produces the expected result.
